verses.1:1: In the second year of the reign of Artaxerxes the great king, on the first day of Nisan, Mordecai, son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin—a Jewish man living in the city of Susa, a great man serving in the court of the king—saw a dream. Now he was from the captivity that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took captive from Jerusalem with Jeconiah the king of Judea. And this was his dream: Look, cries and uproar, thunder and earthquake, turmoil upon the earth. And look, two great dragons came forward, both ready to wrestle; and a great cry came from them, and at their cry every nation was made ready for war so as to make war against a nation of the righteous. And look, a day of darkness and gloom, tribulation and distress, affliction and great turmoil upon the earth; and the whole righteous nation was thrown into turmoil, fearing their own calamities, and they prepared to perish; and they cried out to God. And from their cry there came, as if from a small spring, a great river, much water; light and the sun rose, and the lowly were exalted and devoured the honored ones. And when Mordecai awoke, having seen this dream and what God had purposed to do, he kept it in his heart, and in every way he wanted to understand it until night. And Mordecai rested in the court with Gabatha and Tharra, the two eunuchs of the king who guarded the court; and he heard their reasonings and investigated their concerns, and learned that they were preparing to lay hands on Artaxerxes the king. And he informed the king about them; and the king examined the two eunuchs, and after they confessed, they were led away. And the king wrote these matters as a memorial, and Mordecai wrote about these matters; and the king ordered Mordecai to serve in the court, and gave him gifts for these things. And Haman son of Hammedatha, a Bugaean, was honored before the king, and he sought to harm Mordecai and his people because of the two eunuchs of the king. And it happened after these events, in the days of Artaxerxes—this Artaxerxes ruled over one hundred twenty-seven provinces from India—
verses.1:2: in those very days, when King Artaxerxes was enthroned in the city of Susa,
verses.1:3: in the third year of his reign, he held a banquet for his friends and the rest of the nations and the honored men of the Persians and Medes and the rulers of the satraps.
verses.1:4: And after these things, after he had shown them the wealth of his kingdom and the glory of the gladness of his wealth for one hundred eighty days;
verses.1:5: when the days of the wedding were completed, the king held a drinking feast for the nations who were found in the city for six days in the court of the king's house,
verses.1:6: adorned with fine linen and cotton stretched on cords of fine linen and purple, on cubes of gold and silver, on pillars of Parian marble and stone; couches of gold and silver on a stone pavement of emerald stone and mother-of-pearl and Parian stone, and transparent coverings variously adorned with flowers, with roses strewn all around;
verses.1:7: cups of gold and silver, and a small goblet of carbuncle set out, worth thirty thousand talents; abundant and sweet wine, which the king himself drank.
verses.1:8: Now this drinking feast did not take place according to an established law; rather, so the king wished, and he ordered the stewards to carry out his wish and that of the people.
verses.1:9: And Astin the queen held a drinking feast for the women in the royal palace where King Artaxerxes was.
verses.1:10: And on the seventh day, having become merry, the king told Aman, Mazan, Tharra, Boraze, Zatholtha, Abataza, and Tharaba, the seven eunuchs who were attendants of King Artaxerxes,
verses.1:11: to bring the queen in to him, for her to reign as queen and to put the diadem on her, and to show her to the rulers and to the nations, her beauty, because she was beautiful.
verses.1:12: And Astin the queen did not listen to him to come with the eunuchs; and the king was grieved and became angry,
verses.1:13: and he said to his friends, "Astin has spoken in this way; therefore make a law and a judgment concerning this."
verses.1:14: And Arkesaeus, Sarsathaeus, and Malesear came to him, the rulers of the Persians and Medes who were near the king, the first ones sitting beside the king,
verses.1:15: and they reported to him according to the laws what must be done to Astin the queen, because she did not do the things commanded by the king through the eunuchs.
verses.1:16: And Muchaeus said to the king and the rulers, "Astin the queen has wronged not only the king, but also all the rulers and the leaders of the king."
verses.1:17: For indeed he recounted to them the words of the queen, and how she had contradicted the king. "Just as, then, she contradicted King Artaxerxes,
verses.1:18: so today the rest of the noble ladies of the rulers of the Persians and Medes, having heard the things spoken to the king by her, will dare likewise to dishonor their husbands.
verses.1:19: If, therefore, it seems good to the king, let him issue a royal decree, and let it be written according to the laws of the Medes and Persians, and let him not act otherwise, nor let the queen come in to him anymore; and let the king give her royal position to a woman better than she.
verses.1:20: And let the law from the king, whichever he makes, be heard in his kingdom; and thus all the women will bestow honor on their own husbands, from poor to rich."
verses.1:21: And the word pleased the king and the rulers; and the king did just as Muchaeus had spoken,
verses.1:22: and he sent to all the kingdom, province by province, according to their own language, so that they might be feared in their houses.
verses.2:1: And after these events the king ceased from his wrath, and he no longer remembered Astin, recalling what sorts of things she had spoken and how he had condemned her.
verses.2:2: And the attendants of the king said, "Let uncorrupted young women, beautiful in appearance, be sought for the king;
verses.2:3: and the king will appoint local officials in all the provinces of his kingdom, and let them select virgin young women, beautiful in appearance, into the city of Susa, into the women's quarters, and let them be handed over to the king's eunuch, the guardian of the women, and let ointment and the rest of the care be given;
verses.2:4: and the woman who pleases the king will reign as queen in place of Astin." And the command pleased the king, and he did so.
verses.2:5: And there was a Jewish man in the city of Susa, and his name was Mordecai, son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin,
verses.2:6: who was a captive from Jerusalem, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken captive.
verses.2:7: And he had a foster child, the daughter of Amminadab, his father's brother, and her name was Esther; and when her parents died, he raised her for himself as a wife; and the young woman was beautiful in appearance.
verses.2:8: And when the king's command was heard, many young women were gathered into the city of Susa under the hand of Gai, and Esther was brought to Gai, the guardian of the women.
verses.2:9: And the young woman pleased him, and she found favor before him; and he hurried to give her the ointment and the portion and the seven young women appointed for her from the royal palace, and he treated her and her maidservants well in the women's quarters.
verses.2:10: And Esther did not disclose her race nor her homeland; for Mordecai had commanded her not to report it.
verses.2:11: And every day Mordecai walked around by the women's court, watching to see what would happen to Esther.
verses.2:12: Now this was the time for a young woman to go in to the king, when she had completed twelve months; for thus the days of treatment are completed: six months being anointed with oil of myrrh, and six months with the spices and with the ointments of the women,
verses.2:13: and then she goes in to the king; and to whomever he speaks, he will hand her over to go in with him from the women's quarters to the royal palace.
verses.2:14: In the evening she goes in, and toward daybreak she hurries back to the second women's quarters, where Gai, the king's eunuch, the guardian of the women, is; and she does not go in to the king anymore unless she is called by name.
verses.2:15: And when the time was completed for Esther, the daughter of Amminadab, the brother of Mordecai's father, to go in to the king, she did not disregard anything of what the eunuch, the guardian of the women, had commanded; for Esther was finding favor from all who saw her.
verses.2:16: And Esther went in to Artaxerxes the king in the twelfth month, which is Adar, in the seventh year of his reign.
verses.2:17: And the king fell in love with Esther, and she found favor beyond all the virgins, and he placed the women's diadem on her.
verses.2:18: And the king held a drinking feast for all his friends and the forces for seven days, and he exalted the wedding of Esther, and he granted a remission to those under his kingdom.
verses.2:19: Now Mordecai was serving in the court.
verses.2:20: And Esther did not disclose her homeland; for so Mordecai had commanded her, to fear God and to do His commands, just as when she was with him; and Esther did not change her way of life.
verses.2:21: And the two eunuchs of the king, the chief bodyguards, were grieved because Mordecai had been promoted, and they sought to kill Artaxerxes the king.
verses.2:22: And the matter was made known to Mordecai, and he reported it to Esther, and she revealed the matters of the plot to the king.
verses.2:23: And the king examined the two eunuchs and hanged them; and the king commanded to enter a record as a memorial in the royal library concerning the goodwill of Mordecai, in a commendation.
verses.3:1: And after these things King Artaxerxes honored Haman son of Hammedatha, a Bugaean, and exalted him, and he held the first seat among all his friends.
verses.3:2: And all those in the court were bowing down to him, for so the king had commanded to be done; but Mordecai did not bow down to him.
verses.3:3: And those in the court of the king spoke to Mordecai, "Mordecai, why do you disregard the things spoken by the king?"
verses.3:4: Every day they spoke to him, and he would not listen to them; and they informed Haman that Mordecai was opposing the king's words; and Mordecai had disclosed to them that he was a Jew.
verses.3:5: And when Haman realized that Mordecai did not bow down to him, he became exceedingly furious,
verses.3:6: and he resolved to annihilate all the Jews under the kingdom of Artaxerxes.
verses.3:7: And he made a decree in the twelfth year of the reign of Artaxerxes, and he cast lots day by day and month by month so as to destroy in one day the race of Mordecai; and the lot fell on the fourteenth of the month, which is Adar.
verses.3:8: And he spoke to King Artaxerxes, saying, "There is a nation scattered among the nations in all your kingdom, and their laws are different from all the nations, and they disregard the laws of the king; and it does not benefit the king to leave them alone.
verses.3:9: If it seems good to the king, let him decree to destroy them, and I will pay into the treasury of the king ten thousand talents of silver."
verses.3:10: And the king took off his signet ring and put it into the hand of Haman, to set a seal on the things written against the Jews.
verses.3:11: And the king said to Haman, "Keep the silver, and deal with the nation as you wish."
verses.3:12: And the scribes of the king were summoned in the first month, on the thirteenth day, and they wrote as Haman ordered to the generals and to the rulers in every province from India to Ethiopia, to the one hundred twenty-seven provinces, and to the rulers of the nations according to their own language, by authority of Artaxerxes the king.
verses.3:13: And it was sent through couriers into the kingdom of Artaxerxes, to annihilate the race of the Jews in one day of the twelfth month, which is Adar, and to plunder their possessions. Now this is the copy of the letter: "The great king Artaxerxes writes these things to the rulers and subordinate district governors of the one hundred twenty-seven provinces from India to Ethiopia: Having ruled over many nations and having gained mastery over the whole inhabited world, I purposed—not lifted up by the arrogance of power, but always governing more reasonably and with gentleness—to make the lives of my subjects continually tranquil, and, rendering the kingdom peaceful and passable to its borders, to renew the peace longed for by all people. And when I inquired of my counselors how this might be brought to completion, Haman—who excels among us in soundness of mind, and has been proven unvaryingly in goodwill and steadfast loyalty, and has attained the second honor of the kingdoms—pointed out to us that mixed among all the tribes throughout the inhabited world there is a certain hostile people, opposed in their laws to every nation, and continually disregarding the commands of kings, so that the unified administration blamelessly directed by us is not established. Having understood, therefore, that this nation alone stands continually in opposition to every person, deviating into a strange way of life with its laws, and being ill-disposed toward our affairs, committing the worst evils, even so that the kingdom cannot attain stability; we have commanded, therefore, to destroy all those indicated to you in the things written by Haman, who is appointed over affairs and is our second father, together with wives and children, root and branch, by the swords of their enemies, without any pity or sparing, on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month, Adar, of the present year, so that those who have been hostile both long ago and now, having gone down violently into Hades in one day, may provide us with stable and untroubled affairs continually for the time to come."
verses.3:14: And the copies of the letters were posted province by province; and all the nations were commanded to be ready for this day.
verses.3:15: And the matter was hastened even to Susa; and the king and Haman were carousing, but the city was in turmoil.
verses.4:1: Now when Mordecai learned what was being done, he tore his garments and put on sackcloth and sprinkled ashes on himself; and rushing out through the square of the city, he cried out with a loud voice, "A nation that has done no wrong is being done away with!"
verses.4:2: And he came as far as the king's gate and stopped, for it was not permitted for him to enter the courtyard wearing sackcloth and ashes.
verses.4:3: And in every province where the letters were posted, there was outcry and lamentation and great mourning among the Jews; they spread sackcloth and ashes for themselves.
verses.4:4: And the maids and the eunuchs of the queen came in and reported to her; and she was troubled when she heard what had happened, and she sent to clothe Mordecai and to take away his sackcloth, but he was not persuaded.
verses.4:5: Then Esther summoned Hachrathaeus her eunuch, who attended her, and sent him to learn for her from Mordecai the exact facts.
verses.4:7: And Mordecai showed him what had happened and the promise of ten thousand talents that Haman had promised to the king for the treasury, in order to destroy the Jews.
verses.4:8: And he gave him the copy that was posted in Susa for them to be destroyed, to show to Esther; and he told him to charge her to go in and appeal to the king and petition him on behalf of the people: "Remember the days of your lowliness, how you were brought up by my hand, because Haman, who is second to the king, has spoken against us for death; call upon the Lord and speak to the king on our behalf, and deliver us from death."
verses.4:9: So Hachrathaeus went in and spoke all these words to her.
verses.4:10: And Esther said to Hachrathaeus, "Go to Mordecai and say,
verses.4:11: 'All the nations of the kingdom know that for every man or woman who goes in to the king into the inner courtyard without being called, there is no deliverance; only the one to whom the king extends the golden scepter, this one will be saved. And I have not been called to go in to the king, these thirty days.'"
verses.4:12: And Hachrathaeus reported to Mordecai all the words of Esther.
verses.4:13: And Mordecai said to Hachrathaeus, "Go and say to her, 'Esther, do not say to yourself that you alone will be saved in the kingdom above all the Jews;
verses.4:14: for if you refuse to listen at this time, from another place help and protection will come for the Jews, but you and your father's house will perish. And who knows whether you became queen for this time?'"
verses.4:15: And Esther sent the one who had come to her back to Mordecai, saying,
verses.4:16: "Go, assemble the Jews who are in Susa, and fast for me, and do not eat or drink for three days, night and day; and I also and my maids will abstain from food; and then I will go in to the king contrary to the law, even if I must perish."
verses.4:17: And Mordecai went and did everything that Esther had commanded him. And he prayed to the Lord, remembering all the works of the Lord, and said, "Lord, Lord, King ruling over all, for all things are in Your authority, and there is no one who opposes You when You will to save Israel; for You made heaven and earth and every wondrous thing in the realm under heaven, and You are Lord of all, and there is no one who will resist You, the Lord. You know all things; You know, Lord, that not in insolence nor in pride nor in love of glory did I do this: not bowing down to proud Haman. For I would gladly have kissed the soles of his feet for the deliverance of Israel, but I did this so that I would not place the glory of a man above the glory of God. And I will not bow down to anyone except You, my Lord, and I will not do these things in pride. And now, Lord God, the King, the God of Abraham, spare Your people, for they are looking upon us for ruin and have desired to destroy Your inheritance from the beginning. Do not overlook Your portion, which You redeemed for Yourself out of the land of Egypt. Hear my prayer and be merciful to Your heritage, and turn our mourning into feasting, so that living we may sing praise to Your name, Lord, and do not wipe out the mouth of those who praise You." And all Israel cried out with their strength, because their death was before their eyes. And Esther the queen fled for refuge to the Lord, seized in the agony of death. And taking off her garments of glory, she put on garments of distress and mourning; and instead of the proud perfumes, she filled her head with ashes and dung; and she greatly humbled her body, and every place of her joyful adornment she filled with her tangled hair. And she prayed to the Lord God of Israel and said, "My Lord, our King, You are the only One; help me, who am alone and have no helper except You, because my danger is in my hand. I heard from my birth in the tribe of my paternal family that You, Lord, took Israel out of all the nations, and our fathers out of all their ancestors, for an eternal inheritance, and You did for them all that You spoke. And now we have sinned before You, and You have handed us over into the hands of our enemies, because we glorified their gods. You are righteous, Lord. And now they have not been satisfied with the bitterness of our slavery, but they have set their hands to remove the decree of Your mouth, and to wipe out Your inheritance, and to stop up the mouth of those who praise You, and to extinguish the glory of Your house and Your altar, and to open the mouth of the nations for the praises of worthless things, and for a king of flesh to be marveled at forever. Do not hand over, Lord, Your scepter to those who do not exist, and do not let them laugh at our fall, but turn their counsel upon themselves; and make a public example of the one who began this against us. Remember, Lord; make Yourself known in the time of our affliction, and give me courage, King of the gods, ruling over every dominion. Put well-ordered speech into my mouth before the lion, and turn his heart to hatred of the one who fights against us, to the destruction of him and of those who agree with him. But deliver us by Your hand, and help me, who am alone and have no one except You, Lord. You have knowledge of all things, and You know that I have hated the glory of the lawless, and I abhor the bed of the uncircumcised and of every foreigner. You know my necessity, that I abhor the sign of my pride that is on my head on the days of my appearance; I abhor it like a menstrual cloth, and I do not wear it on the days of my quiet. And Your maidservant has not eaten at Haman's table, and I have not honored a king's banquet, nor have I drunk the wine of libations; and Your maidservant has not rejoiced from the day of my change until now, except in You, Lord God of Abraham. God, who has power over all, hear the voice of those in despair, and deliver us from the hand of the evildoers, and deliver me from my fear."
verses.5:1: And it happened on the third day, when she ceased praying, that she took off the garments of worship and clothed herself in her glory. And having become splendid, after calling upon God, the Overseer of all and Savior, she took along the two maids; and upon the one she leaned as if behaving delicately, while the other followed behind, lifting up her robe. And she herself was blushing at the height of her beauty, and her face was cheerful as if affectionate, yet her heart was constricted with fear. And having passed through all the doors, she stood before the king. And he was sitting on the throne of his kingdom, and he had put on every robe of his splendor, all in gold and precious stones; and he was exceedingly terrifying. And lifting his face, ablaze with glory, he looked in the height of anger; and the queen fell, and her color changed in faintness, and she leaned down upon the head of the maid who was going ahead. Then God changed the spirit of the king into gentleness; and in alarm he sprang up from his throne and took her up into his arms until she recovered, and he comforted her with peaceful words and said to her, "What is it, Esther? I am your brother. Take courage; you will certainly not die, for our decree is a general one. Come near."
verses.5:2: And lifting the golden scepter, he laid it upon her neck, and he embraced her and said, "Speak to me." And she said to him, "I saw you, my lord, like an angel of God, and my heart was troubled from fear of your glory. For you are wondrous, my lord, and your face is full of graces." And while she was speaking, she fell from faintness; and the king was troubled, and all his retinue comforted her.
verses.5:3: And the king said, "What do you want, Esther? And what is your petition? Up to half of my kingdom, and it will be yours."
verses.5:4: And Esther said, "Today is my special day; if therefore it pleases the king, let both him and Haman come to the banquet that I will prepare today."
verses.5:5: And the king said, "Hurry Haman, so that we may carry out Esther's word." And both of them came to the banquet that Esther had mentioned.
verses.5:6: And at the drinking feast, the king said to Esther, "What is it, Queen Esther? And whatever you petition will be done."
verses.5:7: And she said, "My request and petition:
verses.5:8: if I have found favor before the king, let the king and Haman come again tomorrow to the banquet that I will prepare for them, and tomorrow I will do the same."
verses.5:9: And Haman went out from the king overjoyed and rejoicing; but when Haman saw Mordecai the Jew in the courtyard, he became exceedingly angry.
verses.5:10: And going into his own home, he called his friends and Zosara his wife,
verses.5:11: and he showed them his wealth and the honor that the king had bestowed on him, and how he had made him hold first place and lead the kingdom.
verses.5:12: And Haman said, "The queen has invited no one with the king to the banquet except me; and for tomorrow too I have been invited.
verses.5:13: And these things do not please me whenever I see Mordecai the Jew in the courtyard."
verses.5:14: And Zosara his wife and his friends said to him, "Let a pole of fifty cubits be cut for you, and at dawn speak to the king, and let Mordecai be hanged on the pole; and you, go in to the banquet with the king and rejoice." And the word pleased Haman, and the pole was prepared.
verses.6:1: Now the Lord removed sleep from the king that night, and he told his instructor to bring in memorial records of the days to read to him.
verses.6:2: And he found the records written concerning Mordecai, how he had reported to the king concerning the two eunuchs of the king, when they were keeping guard and sought to lay hands on Artaxerxes.
verses.6:3: And the king said, "What honor or favor have we done for Mordecai?" And the servants of the king said, "You have done nothing for him."
verses.6:4: Now while the king was inquiring about Mordecai's goodwill, look, Haman was in the courtyard. And the king said, "Who is in the courtyard?" Now Haman had come in to tell the king to hang Mordecai on the pole that he had prepared.
verses.6:5: And the servants of the king said, "Look, Haman is standing in the courtyard." And the king said, "Call him."
verses.6:6: And the king said to Haman, "What should I do for the man whom I wish to honor?" And Haman said within himself, "Whom does the king wish to honor except me?"
verses.6:7: And he said to the king, "For a man whom the king wishes to honor,
verses.6:8: let the king's attendants bring a fine linen robe that the king wears, and a horse on which the king rides,
verses.6:9: and let him give them to one of the illustrious friends of the king, and let him clothe the man whom the king loves, and mount him on the horse, and let him proclaim through the square of the city, saying, 'Thus it will be for every man whom the king honors.'"
verses.6:10: And the king said to Haman, "You have spoken well. Do so for Mordecai the Jew, who serves in the courtyard, and let no word of yours fail from what you have spoken."
verses.6:11: So Haman took the robe and the horse, and clothed Mordecai and mounted him on the horse, and went through the square of the city and kept proclaiming, saying, "Thus it will be for every man whom the king wishes to honor."
verses.6:12: Then Mordecai returned to the courtyard, while Haman went back to his own home, grieving with his head covered.
verses.6:13: And Haman recounted what had happened to him to Zosara his wife and to his friends. And his friends and his wife said to him, "If Mordecai is of the race of the Jews, you have begun to be humbled before him; you will surely fall. You will by no means be able to defend yourself against him, because a living God is with him."
verses.6:14: While they were still speaking, the eunuchs arrived, hurrying Haman to the drinking feast that Esther had prepared.
verses.7:1: Now the king and Haman went in to drink with the queen.
verses.7:2: And the king said to Esther on the second day during the drinking banquet, "What is it, Queen Esther, and what is your request, and what is your petition? And let it be yours, up to half of my kingdom."
verses.7:3: And answering, she said, "If I have found favor before the king, let my life be given at my request, and my word at my petition.
verses.7:4: For we have been sold, both I and my people, for destruction and plunder and slavery, we and our children as male and female servants, and I disregarded it; for the slanderer is not worthy of the king's court."
verses.7:5: And the king said, "Who is this who dared to do this thing?"
verses.7:6: And Esther said, "A hostile man, this wicked Haman." And Haman was terrified before the king and the queen.
verses.7:7: And the king rose up from the banquet and went into the garden; and Haman was pleading with the queen, for he saw that he was in trouble.
verses.7:8: And the king returned from the garden, and Haman had fallen upon the couch, petitioning the queen; and the king said, "So are you even assaulting my wife in my house?" And when Haman heard this, he was confounded in his face.
verses.7:9: And Bougathan, one of the eunuchs, said to the king, "Look, Haman has even prepared a wooden pole for Mordecai, the one who spoke concerning the king, and a wooden pole of fifty cubits stands upright on Haman's property." And the king said, "Let him be crucified on it."
verses.7:10: And Haman was hanged on the wooden pole that had been prepared for Mordecai. And then the king ceased from his wrath.
verses.8:1: And on that very day King Artaxerxes bestowed on Esther all that belonged to Haman the slanderer, and Mordecai was summoned by the king; for Esther had revealed that he was related to her.
verses.8:2: And the king took the signet ring that he had taken away from Haman and gave it to Mordecai, and Esther appointed Mordecai over all the property of Haman.
verses.8:3: And she spoke once more to the king, and fell at his feet, and petitioned him to remove the malice of Haman and all that he had done to the Jews.
verses.8:4: And the king extended the golden scepter to Esther; and Esther rose up to stand before the king.
verses.8:5: And Esther said, "If it seems good to you and I have found favor, let word be sent that the letters sent by Haman be revoked, those written that the Jews who are in your kingdom should perish.
verses.8:6: For how will I be able to see the affliction of my people, and how will I be able to be saved in the destruction of my homeland?"
verses.8:7: And the king said to Esther, "If I have given and graciously granted to you all the possessions of Haman, and have hanged him on a wooden pole because he laid hands on the Jews, what more do you seek?
verses.8:8: You also write in my name as seems good to you, and seal it with my signet ring; for whatever is written at the king's command and is sealed with my signet ring cannot be contradicted."
verses.8:9: And the scribes were summoned in the first month, which is Nisan, on the twenty-third of the same year, and it was written to the Jews, all that he commanded to the stewards and to the rulers of the satraps from India to Ethiopia, to one hundred twenty-seven satrapies, province by province, according to their own language.
verses.8:10: And it was written through the king and sealed with his signet ring, and they sent out the letters by couriers,
verses.8:11: as he commanded them to observe their laws in every city, and to come to their own aid and to deal with their adversaries and their opponents as they wished,
verses.8:12: on one day throughout the whole kingdom of Artaxerxes, on the thirteenth of the twelfth month, which is Adar. Of these things, the following is the copy of the letter: "The Great King Artaxerxes to the rulers of the provinces in the one hundred twenty-seven satrapies from India to Ethiopia, and to those who are loyal to our interests, greetings. Many, being honored more frequently through the abundant kindness of those who confer benefits, have grown too proud, and not only do they seek to harm those who are subject to us, but being unable to bear their excess, they even undertake to scheme against their own benefactors; and not only removing gratitude from among people, but also puffed up by the boasts of those ignorant of goodness, they suppose that they will escape the evil-hating justice of God, who always sees all things. Often also, the persuasion of friends entrusted to manage affairs has made many of those appointed to positions of authority partakers of innocent blood and plunged them into irremediable calamities, when with the false reasoning of malice they misled the sincere goodwill of those who hold power. Now it is possible to observe, not so much from the older histories as we have handed down, as when you examine what lies right at hand, how many things have been impiously perpetrated by the pestilent wickedness of those who wield power unworthily, and to pay attention to what comes afterward, so that we may render the kingdom undisturbed for all people with peace, making use of the changes, and always judging the matters that come before our eyes with a more equitable response. For thus Haman son of Hammedatha, a Macedonian, in truth an alien to Persian blood and far removed from our kindness, having been received as a guest by us, obtained the benevolence that we hold toward every nation to such a degree that he was publicly proclaimed our father and, bowed down to by all, continued as the second person to the royal throne; yet, unable to restrain his arrogance, he endeavored to deprive us of our rule and our life, demanding for destruction, through intricate false reasonings of craftiness, both Mordecai, our savior and continual benefactor, and Esther, the blameless partner of the kingdom, together with their entire nation; for by these means he thought, having caught us isolated, to transfer the dominion of the Persians to the Macedonians. But we find that the Jews, who were handed over to annihilation by that thrice-wicked man, are not evildoers, but live under the most righteous laws and are sons of the Most High, Greatest, Living God, who directs the kingdom for both us and our ancestors in the finest order. You will therefore do well not to act upon the letters sent by Haman son of Hammedatha, because the very one who perpetrated these things has been crucified at the gates of Susa with his entire household, since God, who rules over all things, has swiftly rendered to him the judgment he deserved; and having posted the copy of this letter openly in every place, permit the Jews to observe their own customs, and lend them support so that they may defend themselves against those who attack them in the time of distress on the thirteenth of the twelfth month, Adar, on that very day; for God, who holds dominion over all things, has made this day gladness for them instead of destruction for the chosen race. Therefore you also, among your named festivals, observe a notable day with all feasting, so that both now and afterward it may be deliverance for us and for the well-disposed Persians, but for those who plot against us, a memorial of destruction. And every city or province without exception that does not act according to these things will be consumed with spear and fire in wrath; not only impassable to humans, it will also be rendered most hateful to wild beasts and birds for all time."
verses.8:13: And the copies were to be posted in full view throughout the whole kingdom, and all the Jews were to be ready for this day to fight against their foes.
verses.8:14: So the horsemen went out, hastening to carry out what was spoken by the king; and the decree was also posted in Susa.
verses.8:15: And Mordecai went out clothed in the royal robe, wearing a golden crown and a purple diadem of fine linen; and when those in Susa saw him, they rejoiced.
verses.8:16: And for the Jews there was light and gladness,
verses.8:17: in every city and province wherever the decree was posted, wherever the proclamation was posted: joy and gladness for the Jews, a banquet and gladness; and many of the nations were circumcised and lived as Jews because of the fear of the Jews.
verses.9:1: For in the twelfth month, on the thirteenth of the month, which is Adar, the letters written by the king arrived.
verses.9:2: On that very day the opponents of the Jews perished; for no one resisted, fearing them.
verses.9:3: For the rulers of the satraps and the governors and the royal scribes honored the Jews; for the fear of Mordecai lay upon them.
verses.9:4: For the decree of the king had arrived to be spoken of throughout the whole kingdom.
verses.9:6: And in that very city the Jews killed five hundred men,
verses.9:7: both Pharsan and Nestain and Delphon and Phasga,
verses.9:8: and Pharadatha and Barsa and Sarbacha,
verses.9:9: and Marmasima and Rouphaeus and Arsaeus and Zabouthaeus,
verses.9:10: the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, the Bugaean, the enemy of the Jews; and they took plunder
verses.9:11: on that very day; and the number of those who had perished in Susa was submitted to the king.
verses.9:12: And the king said to Esther, "The Jews have destroyed five hundred men in the city of Susa; and in the surrounding region, how do you think they have acted? What more, then, do you petition, and it will be yours?"
verses.9:13: And Esther said to the king, "Let it be granted to the Jews to act likewise tomorrow, so as to hang the ten sons of Haman."
verses.9:14: And he permitted it to be done so, and he handed over to the Jews of the city the bodies of the sons of Haman to hang.
verses.9:15: And the Jews in Susa gathered together on the fourteenth of Adar and killed three hundred men, and they plundered nothing.
verses.9:16: And the rest of the Jews who were in the kingdom gathered together and came to their own aid, and rested from their foes; for they destroyed fifteen thousand of them on the thirteenth of Adar, and they plundered nothing.
verses.9:17: And they rested on the fourteenth of the same month, and observed it as a day of rest with joy and gladness.
verses.9:18: But the Jews who were in the city of Susa gathered together on the fourteenth as well and did not rest; and they also observed the fifteenth with joy and gladness.
verses.9:19: For this reason, therefore, the Jews who are scattered in every outlying province observe the fourteenth of Adar as a good day with gladness, sending portions each to his neighbor. And those who dwell in the metropolises also observe the fifteenth of Adar as a good festivity, sending out portions to their neighbors as well.
verses.9:20: And Mordecai wrote these words in a book, and sent them out to all the Jews who were in the kingdom of Artaxerxes, to those near and to those far away,
verses.9:21: to establish these days as good days, and to observe the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar;
verses.9:22: for on these days the Jews rested from their enemies; and to observe the whole month in which it was turned for them, which was Adar, from mourning into joy and from grief into a good day, as good days of wedding feasts and gladness, sending out portions to friends and to the poor.
verses.9:23: And the Jews accepted just as Mordecai had written to them,
verses.9:24: how Haman son of Hammedatha, the Macedonian, waged war against them, just as he had set a decree and a lot to annihilate them,
verses.9:25: and how he went in to the king, saying to hang Mordecai; but all the evils that he undertook to bring upon the Jews came upon him, and both he himself and his children were hanged.
verses.9:26: Therefore these days were called Phrourai because of the lots, because in their language they are called Phrourai, because of the words of this letter, and all that they had suffered because of these things, and all that had happened to them,
verses.9:27: and he established it; and the Jews accepted it upon themselves and upon their offspring and upon those joined to them, and they will certainly not act otherwise. And these days are a memorial observed generation after generation, and in every city, family, and province.
verses.9:28: And these days of Phrourai will be observed for all time, and their memorial will never fail from the generations.
verses.9:29: And Queen Esther, daughter of Amminadab, and Mordecai the Jew wrote all that they had done and the confirmation of the letter of Phrourai.
verses.9:31: And Mordecai and Queen Esther established it for themselves upon themselves, and at that time established their counsel as well, against their own health.
verses.9:32: And Esther established it by word forever, and it was written for a memorial.
verses.10:1: Now the king wrote to the kingdom of the land and of the sea.
verses.10:2: And as for his strength and valor, both the wealth and the glory of his kingdom, look, it is written in the book of the kings of the Persians and Medes as a memorial.
verses.10:3: And Mordecai acted as deputy to King Artaxerxes, and was great in the kingdom and honored by the Jews; and being loved, he set forth the way of life to all his nation. And Mordecai said, "These things came from God. For I remembered the dream that I saw concerning these matters, for not even a single matter among them passed away: the little spring that became a river, and there was light and sun and much water. Esther is the river, whom the king married and made queen; and the two dragons are I and Haman; and the nations are those who were gathered together to destroy the name of the Jews; and as for my nation, this is Israel, who cried out to God and were saved. And the Lord saved His people, and the Lord delivered us from all these evils; and God performed the signs and the great wonders that have not happened among the nations. For this reason He made two lots, one for the people of God and one for all the nations; and these two lots came to the hour and time and to the day of judgment before God and for all the nations, and God remembered His people and vindicated His own inheritance. And these days will be for them in the month of Adar, on the fourteenth and on the fifteenth of the same month, with assembly and joy and gladness before God throughout the generations forever among His people Israel." In the fourth year of the reign of Ptolemy and Cleopatra, Dositheus, who said he was a priest and a Levite, and Ptolemy his son brought in the preceding letter of Phrourai; they said it was genuine and that Lysimachus, son of Ptolemy, one of those in Jerusalem, had translated it.

notes.1:1: Includes the Septuagint prologue (Addition A) narrating Mordecai's dream and his discovery of the plot by Gabatha and Tharra (distinct from Bigthan and Teresh in Hebrew 2:21). Throughout the book, the Greek names the king Artaxerxes (Hebrew Ahasuerus) and calls Haman a Bugaean (Greek Bougaios, Hebrew Agagite), and here notes one hundred twenty-seven provinces "from India" without adding "to Ethiopia."
notes.1:5: The Greek specifies "the days of the wedding" (Hebrew "these days") and gives the banquet's duration as "six days" (Hebrew "seven days"), although 1:10 refers to "the seventh day."
notes.1:9: Greek Astin is the Septuagint form of the queen's name, corresponding to Vashti in the Hebrew text.
notes.1:10: The Greek names of the seven eunuchs (Aman, Mazan, Tharra, Boraze, Zatholtha, Abataza, and Tharaba) differ markedly from the Hebrew list; likewise 1:14 names only three rulers (Arkesaeus, Sarsathaeus, and Malesear) instead of seven, and 1:16 names Muchaeus (Hebrew Memucan).
notes.1:17: The opening clause is a narratorial parenthesis explaining that Muchaeus recounted the queen's words to the rulers before his direct speech resumes in the second clause.
notes.2:1: The Greek states that the king "no longer remembered Astin," directly contrasting with the Hebrew text ("remembered Vashti").
notes.2:7: The Greek names Esther's father Amminadab (Hebrew Abihail in 2:15) and states that Mordecai raised Esther "for himself as a wife" (Greek eis gynaika), whereas the Hebrew reads "as his own daughter."
notes.2:8: Greek Gai corresponds to Hebrew Hegai; in 2:14 the Greek again names Gai as guardian of the second women's quarters, where the Hebrew names Shaashgaz.
notes.2:13: The Greek wording differs from the Hebrew, describing the guardian handing the young woman over to whichever designated escort is instructed to bring her to the royal palace.
notes.2:16: The Greek dates Esther's entry to the king to "the twelfth month, which is Adar" (Hebrew "the tenth month, Tebeth"); in 2:20 the Greek also adds Mordecai's command "to fear God and to do His commands."
notes.3:7: The Greek notes that Haman made a decree and that the lot fell on the fourteenth of Adar (matching Addition B in 3:13), whereas the Hebrew sets the date on the thirteenth of Adar in 3:13.
notes.3:13: Includes the Septuagint text of the royal edict (Addition B), composed in formal Hellenistic chancery style, fixing the destruction for the fourteenth of Adar and depicting the victims descending violently into Hades.
notes.4:5: "Hachrathaeus" is the Septuagint name (Greek Hachrathaios) of Esther's eunuch, corresponding to Hathach in the Hebrew Masoretic Text. The Greek text also omits verse 4:6.
notes.4:14: The Greek reads "if you refuse to listen" (parakouses), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "if you remain silent."
notes.4:16: Literally "even if it should be for me to perish," reflecting the Septuagint wording rather than the Hebrew "if I perish, I perish."
notes.4:17: In the Septuagint, verse 4:17 incorporates the prayers of Mordecai and Esther (traditionally called Addition C). In Esther's prayer, "my change" refers to her change of status upon entering the palace, and this text reads simply "they have set their hands" without the longer clause found in some manuscripts.
notes.5:1: Verses 5:1-2 preserve the expanded Septuagint account of Esther's audience before the king (traditionally called Addition D). "Our decree is a general one" (Greek koinon, literally "common" or "public") means that the law applies to ordinary subjects rather than to the queen.
notes.5:4: "Today is my special day" (Greek episemos, "notable" or "festive") is unique to the Septuagint and has no counterpart in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.5:10: "Zosara" is the Septuagint name of Haman's wife, corresponding to Zeresh in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.5:14: Greek xylon literally means "wood," "beam," or "pole" (used for hanging or impaling), traditionally rendered "gallows."
notes.6:1: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("sleep fled from the king"), the Septuagint explicitly credits the Lord with removing the king's sleep; "his instructor" translates Greek didaskalos ("teacher"), denoting the royal reader or chronicler.
notes.6:2: Throughout the Septuagint of Esther, the Persian king is named Artaxerxes rather than Ahasuerus as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.6:12: "With his head covered" renders the idiomatic Greek phrase kata kephales (literally "down over [his] head"), an elliptical expression for covering one's head in grief or shame.
notes.6:13: "Because a living God is with him" is a theological statement distinctive to the Septuagint; the anarthrous Greek phrase theos zon ("a living God") can also be rendered "the living God."
notes.7:3: The Greek text reads ho logos mou ("my word") rather than ho laos mou ("my people"), and has he psyche ("my life") without an explicit possessive pronoun.
notes.7:4: The Septuagint distinctively adds "and slavery" and renders Esther's statement "and I disregarded it; for the slanderer (ho diabolos) is not worthy of the king's court," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.7:8: The Greek reads "he was confounded in his face" (dietrape to prosopo), rather than the Hebrew "they covered Haman's face."
notes.7:9: "Bougathan" is the Septuagint name of the eunuch (corresponding to Harbonah in the Hebrew); Greek xylon ("wooden pole") and stauroo ("be crucified/impaled") reflect Hellenistic execution terminology.
notes.8:1: The Septuagint consistently names the Persian king "Artaxerxes" rather than "Ahasuerus."
notes.8:9: The Septuagint dates the decree to "the first month, which is Nisan" (Greek Nisa), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the third month, which is Sivan."
notes.8:12: This verse incorporates the full text of Artaxerxes's royal letter (known as Addition E in the Greek tradition), which identifies Haman as "a Macedonian" rather than an Agagite and has no counterpart in the Hebrew text.
notes.8:17: The Septuagint preserves a doublet ("wherever the decree was posted, wherever the proclamation was posted") and explicitly adds that many of the nations "were circumcised" (perietemonto) and "lived as Jews" (ioudaizon).
notes.9:4: The Greek compresses this verse ("For the decree of the king had arrived to be spoken of throughout the whole kingdom") and omits verse 5 entirely compared to the Hebrew text.
notes.9:10: Verses 7-9 list eleven Greek forms for the names of Haman's "ten sons" (splitting the first name into Pharsan and Nestain) and call Haman "the Bugaean"; uniquely, the Greek text also reads "and they took plunder" (kai dierpasan) without a negation.
notes.9:16: The Septuagint reads "fifteen thousand" (myrious pentakischilious), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads seventy-five thousand.
notes.9:26: "Phrourai" is the Septuagint form of the festival name Purim (and in 9:29 Esther's father is named "Amminadab" rather than Abihail).
notes.9:31: Verse 30 is absent in the Septuagint, and verse 31 has compressed Greek syntax stating that Mordecai and Esther established their counsel "against their own health" (kata tes hygieias heauton), corresponding to the Hebrew mention of fasting and lamentation.
notes.10:1: The Greek text here has no explicit direct object after "wrote" (literally "wrote to/upon the kingdom"). Some Septuagint manuscripts add "taxes" here (compare the Hebrew, "laid tribute upon the land").
notes.10:3: As throughout Greek Esther, the king is named Artaxerxes (Hebrew Ahasuerus), and the Greek extends the verse with Mordecai's dream interpretation and the translator's colophon; "set forth the way of life" reflects a debated Greek phrase differing from the Hebrew. In the colophon, "Phrourai" is the Septuagint form of Purim, and "was genuine" renders the Greek verb "to be" used absolutely.
